  They'll develop that gray-green ring around the yolk if they sit too long, which is
  harmless but a sign they're getting old.

transcript.user: nice. any tips for jet lag in general?
transcript.answer:
Key moves:

  • Adjust sleep before you go. A few days before, shift your bedtime closer to Portugal
  time (3 hours ahead of Chicago). Even an hour helps.
  • Daylight on arrival. Get outside in sunlight as soon as you land—it resets your
  circadian rhythm faster than anything. October sun in Lisbon is perfect for this.
  • Melatonin strategically. Take it a few hours before your target bedtime in Portugal,
  starting the night before travel. Helps you sleep on the plane and adjust faster.
  • Skip naps. Stay awake until local bedtime that first night, no matter how brutal.
  One miserable evening beats being jet-lagged for days.
  • Hydrate + move. Drink water on the plane, walk around. Dehydration makes jet lag
  worse.
  • Caffeine timing. Have it in the morning in your new timezone, none after 2pm local
  time.

  Honest take: With a 3-hour difference, you're lucky—it's not brutal. Most people
  adjust
  in 1–2 days naturally. The "stay awake until bedtime" rule is the real difference-
  maker.
